newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Dec 10.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Dec 10.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

Coles Myer Ltd on Monday announced the surprise resignation of managing director Peter Bartels, the highest paid chief executive in the country. Bartels will be replaced by Dennis Eck, Coles Myer's chief operating officer of the company's business units division. Analysts said Eck's retailing pedigree appeared solid but they said the new chief executive's department store skills were unproven.

Santos Ltd said on Monday it would maintain its focus on exploration, spending at least $150 million in calendar 1997 from A$130 million this year and A$88 million last year. Managing director Ross Adler told a Securities Institute of Australia briefing that Santos would drill close to its 1996 target of 99 wells for the year.
* Mt Edon Gold Mines NL A$1.60 (unch)

Westgold Resources NL, which earlier on Monday said it increased its stake in Mount Edon Gold Mines NL to 6.75 percent, would consider a takeover bid for the Western Australian gold producer, Westgold chairman Mladen Ninkov told Reuters. "We're always looking at our options, which may include a friendly (takeover)," Ninkov said late on Monday.

Consoldiated Rutile Ltd said on Monday it would raise A$96.4 million through a 19-for-10 rights issue to fund a fully franked dividend of A$1.62 per share, which will cost A$96.7 million. The Brisbane-based mineral sands miner said the dividend will release substantial franking credits to shareholders, an issue it referred to at the annual meeting on November 6.

Novus Petroleum Ltd said on Monday the Southeast Sumatra production sharing contract (psc) in Indonesia was currently producing crude oil at an average rate of 153,000 barrels a day, up 12 percent from the 1995 average.

Advertising agency Singleton Group Ltd said on Monday it planned a special fully franked dividend payment of about A$1.80 per share following the sale of its 10 percent voting stake in the television network Ten Group Ltd.

Oil Search Ltd said on Monday that tests had shown two oil bearing intervals in its Moran 1X/Sidetrack 4 exploration well onshore in Papua New Guinea. Electric logs indicated that the Toro interval and the upper part of the Digimu sandstone were oil bearing, it said.
